text: Sunday morning, Mok is on every channel in handcuffs. The man who loved cameras can't face one.
Black Hound loses its licence. The guild that called him trap rat leaves in cardboard boxes.
And Kanghan does as Director Baek ordered, burying Black Hound in one sentence: Mok was never theirs.
The radish granny isn't buying a word of it.
Back home, Jaeha sleeps under a fat cat. His body paid for every blow Nib took.
Then the phone buzzes across the floorboards, and a hand creeps out to find it. The Association, calling about the money.
The core is locked up until the trial, so the money waits. Jaeha thanks them, mostly asleep.
Lyra spins round at the word money. She has wanted her cut since she arrived. It's locked up too.
She flops back, despairing of the human world. Nib, for once, agrees.
Then Seoa smacks him with a pillow and won't let go of his sleeve. The pillow is anger. The hand is fear.
That afternoon, Jaeha limps on a stick into a quiet columbarium, Nib beside him.
Behind one small glass door: an urn, a can of coffee, a tiny wooden husk, and Minseok's photo.
Jaeha takes off his cap. He finally has news for hyung: the man who shut him in is in handcuffs.
He presses a thumbs-up sticker on the glass, like the one on hyung's phone.
Nib asks a soldier's question. Jaeha gives a trap-tester's answer: hyung was no stronger than him, and went first anyway.
Nib lifts his mask to see the photo with his own eyes. He'd have liked him, and from Nib, that's high praise.
Then Choi arrives with two coffees. He still remembers how Minseok took his, and still disapproves.
Jaeha had no idea. They've mourned the same man every year, hours apart, and never once met.
He holds out an old USB stick. The phone is locked away, but Choi kept a copy.
Choi won't say how he revived a dead phone. Jaeha's question is worse: if hyung died inside, how did Mok get it?
Choi's smile fades. Four years ago, a Black Hound man helped him with the screaming kid, and searched his pockets.
And the colour drains out of Jaeha's eyes.
In grey: Choi watches the kid. The other man watches the door, and slips an orange phone from the kid's vest. Young Mok.
Jaeha's hand goes to his chest. Hyung wasn't only pushing him out. He was sending him something.
Choi pats his shoulder on his way out. Late, but delivered. See you at dinner.
Nib quietly holds the hem of Jaeha's hoodie.
That evening, the whole crew crowds onto the rooftop for tteokbokki.
Borro holds out a crate of lettuce from his tarp garden, so proud that flowers pop open on his shell.
Nib treats it like enemy rations and demands a taster. Seoa's protest only makes her more suspicious.
So Seoa takes one for the team.
Safety confirmed, Nib eats half the crate.
Then Bomi shoots out of her chair like a firework. Her channel just crossed a million.
And Saturday's two million viewers didn't just watch. They gave forty-eight million won.
Bomi splits it four ways, with his husks as a full share. Jaeha tries to refuse. Too late.
His share and the husks': twenty-four million won. It's also his entire balance.
Lyra clutches her heart. Finally, a human who pays.
Seoa does the sums: art school and a year's rent, just what the core was for. Even the landlady warms to the pets.
Nib objects to his new job title.
On the water tank, Lyra lounges against the dusk like it was painted for her. Her review of soju: mixed.
Jaeha looks very hard the other way. Nib stares at him.
Then Lyra sits beside him, serious. Finding her brother was part of her price. He says soon. She's heard that before.
Yerin shyly admits she held it together this time. Jaeha knows. He rode out on her back.
Jaeha looks around at them all. Everyone comes back: hyung's rule held, this time. Just not for hyung.
Late that night, Borro sleeps by his garden, the cat on his shell.
Across the city, a gloved hand flicks a silver baton.
In Kanghan's hall, the woman in white who once spotted Nib in a clip conducts forty husks alone.
One expense on her tablet doesn't add up. Kanghan pays a crew of trap-testers every week, cash in hand.
Officially, Kanghan has no gate on the Han. So what are those people surveying?
Forty husks lower their arms as one, and she looks out toward the river.
Hours later, Lyra snores in a blanket burrito, and Jaeha sits at the laptop with the USB.
On the spillway, the phone cut out at two thirty-one. The file runs sixteen seconds longer.
After the line everyone heard, Minseok's crooked grin comes back. Even now, he's worried the kid doesn't eat.
Then he glances behind the phone, and decides the kid should know where they are.
The camera swings round.
Through the shimmer of the gate's rim: a Han River bridge pier, a faded yellow seven, one cracked lamp.
The frozen pier shines in Jaeha's eyes.
He knows that pier. He saw it through Nib's eyes the night the cat chased him there. Kanghan guards it.
He whispers the question to Nib. Nib is certain at once, down to the cracked lamp.
So he checks the Association's record. On paper, the raid that killed hyung also closed this gate for good.
Nib frowns. The record and his own eyes can't both be right. A scout trusts his eyes.
His ears go flat. Every child knows the rule: no gate shuts while its boss is breathing.
Jaeha turns to an old page: Mok, Minseok, Han River. Mok gets crossed out. Underneath: a boss that never died.
He closes the notebook. Four years open is no accident. Someone wants it that way.
From the roof, half a kilometre away, a cold glow under one bridge pier. Hyung's gate, visible from home.
And far away under the bridge, the glow pulses once, slowly, like a heartbeat.
